keyMessage.found: CMC lists hardware and medical devices but not software, cloud services, or data flows, and assets lack owners and criticality.
keyMessage.closes: Build a software and cloud inventory and map patient data flows.

categories.whatWorksToday: Hardware and medical device inventories exist, and cloud applications are partly known.

strengths.statement: Hardware and medical device inventories exist, and the hardware inventory was demonstrated.
Cloud and SaaS applications are partly known, a start for a full software inventory.
The medical device inventory records operating system version and network location, a base for criticality ranking.

gapFindings.title: Software, cloud, and data-flow inventories are missing
gapFindings.statement: CMC lists hardware and medical devices but not software, cloud services, or data flows, so exposure and breach scope cannot be mapped.

supportingFacts.fact: No software inventory shows versions and support status.
Cloud and SaaS applications bought by departments are only partly known.
Network and data flow diagrams were not confirmed.

extent.notChecked: Number of unlisted cloud services is unknown

gapFindings.consequence: Unlisted software stays unpatched, and after a breach CMC cannot say which patient records left the hospital.

likelihood.rationale: Inventory is Weak on Criticality A systems.

ops.rationale: Unscoped breach stops or slows hospital operations.

fin.rationale: Unscoped breach adds recovery cost and revenue loss.

legal.rationale: Unscoped breach triggers reporting duties or regulator questions.

rep.rationale: Unscoped breach damages patient and public trust.

safety.rationale: Unscoped breach delays or disrupts patient care.

data.rationale: Unscoped breach exposes sensitive health records.

notApplicable.prevent: Recurrence is addressed by the related Governance and Process actions.
notApplicable.exceptions: No system is known to be unable to meet the control.

gapFindings.title: Asset ownership, criticality, and disposal are not managed
gapFindings.statement: Assets lack owners and criticality in the inventory, and devices leave CMC without disk sanitization.

supportingFacts.fact: Unknown devices connecting to the network are handled informally.
Disks and devices are not sanitized before disposal or vendor return.
PACS and Active Directory have an IT owner only.

gapFindings.consequence: Patient data on a returned disk reaches a third party, and unknown devices join the network unnoticed.

likelihood.rationale: Controls are Partial on Criticality A assets.

ops.rationale: Data on a returned disk stops or slows hospital operations.

fin.rationale: Limited direct effect in this scenario.

keyMessage.found: Internal systems are not scanned, the exposed website runs an unsupported PHP version, and threat information plays no part in risk ratings.
keyMessage.closes: Run monthly authenticated scans on Criticality A systems and the website, and write ransomware threat scenarios.

strengths.statement: Application code is scanned and tested before go-live, and a vulnerability process is documented.

gapFindings.title: Internal systems are not scanned and the website carries a known weakness
gapFindings.statement: CMC does not scan its internal systems for vulnerabilities, so known flaws stay open until an outsider finds them.

supportingFacts.fact: No authenticated vulnerability scans run on internal systems.
The hospital website shows an unsupported PHP version and an internet-reachable admin login.
Vendor advisories and exploited-flaw alerts are tracked only in part.

extent.notChecked: Scan coverage of LIS and ERP was not confirmed

gapFindings.consequence: Attackers use a known flaw on the website or an internal server to gain a foothold and move toward HIS.

likelihood.rationale: No scanning exists on Criticality A systems, an internet-facing weakness is open, and the threat is active.

gapFindings.title: Threats and risk responses are not recorded or tracked
gapFindings.statement: CMC likely rates risks without sector threat information, so it has not judged its exposure to the ransomware that hit a peer hospital.

supportingFacts.fact: No record lists internal and external threats.
Threat intelligence is received only informally.
Third-party components in HIS and the website are not tracked.

extent.notChecked: Use of threat feeds by IT was not reviewed

gapFindings.consequence: Controls are chosen without a view of the likely attack path, so spending misses the routes attackers actually use.

improvementActions.action: Build a software and cloud service inventory with version and support status, Criticality A systems first
Map network and patient data flows for HIS, PACS, LIS, and ERP and start the Record of Processing Activities (ROPA)
Assign an owner and criticality to every hardware and medical device record
Require inventory update in change approval and reconcile it every six months
Run authenticated vulnerability scans monthly on Criticality A systems and the hospital website and track findings to closure
Set remediation timelines by severity and report them to the steering committee
Write ransomware and third-party access threat scenarios from the peer hospital incident
Subscribe to a sector threat advisory source and review it monthly
Run a first tabletop exercise on ransomware and record the improvements
Open an improvement register fed by exercises, audits, and incidents
